title: QBR Segmentation Mosaic: Workbench for Renewal Prioritization
content:
Purpose:
This working document is a lightweight, reusable workbench to: 1) score and segment accounts for QBR prioritization, 2) synthesize renewal risk and NRR upside, and 3) output targeted playbook actions by segment. Designed for weekly CS triage and QBR prep across regions and deployment modes.

Overview & design principles:
- Signal-first: combine quantitative signals (usage, latency SLO breaches, spend velocity) with qualitative signals (exec interest, recent escalations).
- Multi-dimensional segmentation: not just revenue tier — we score across ICP fit, deployment mode risk/complexity, and region-specific renewal dynamics.
- Actionable output: each account maps to a single QBR priority and a set of 1-3 recommended playbook actions.
- Lightweight and exportable: can be maintained in a sheet and snapshot into QBR slides.

Scoring model (single-number priority score):
- Tier score (0-40): based on ARR/commit and strategic importance. (Tier S = 40, Tier A = 30, B = 20, C = 10)
- ICP fit (0-25): 0 low fit -> 25 ideal fit. Factors: product line match, feature dependency (e.g., private deployment required), public case studies potential.
- Deployment mode friction (0-20): higher value = greater operational risk (Private on-prem = 20, VPC = 15, Dedicated = 10, Hosted = 5). This is expressed as risk multiplier; we add points for complexity to prioritize follow-up.
- Region modifier (0-5): APAC adjustments and contract cadence differences (APAC +3 if contract timelines misalign, EU +2 if GDPR review pending).
- Health offset (-20 to +10): negative for clear churn signals (support tickets unresolved >14d, usage drop >60%), positive for CS-led upsell activity.

Priority score = Tier + ICP fit + Deployment mode + Region modifier + Health offset.
Normalize into buckets: High (>=70), Medium (45-69), Low (<45).

Fields to populate per account (sheet columns):
- Account name
- Owner (CSM)
- ARR / committed MRR
- Tier (S/A/B/C)
- ICP fit score (0-25) + short rationale
- Deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / VPC / On‑prem)
- Deployment friction score (0-20)
- Region (NA / EMEA / APAC) + region modifier applied
- Health delta: last 90d usage % change + critical tickets count
- Health offset applied (-20..+10) + rationale
- Priority score (numeric)
- Priority bucket (High/Medium/Low)
- Next 90d recommended actions (1-3 bullets)
- Suggested QBR owners / stakeholders (e.g., solutions-eng, account exec)
- Renewal date & current contract terms
- Estimated NRR impact (USD range)
- Recent engagement notes (free text)

Example rows (illustrative):
1) Blackbird Retail
- Owner: Maya Chen
- ARR: $420k
- Tier: A (30)
- ICP fit: 22 (strong retail-specific embedding use)
- Deployment: VPC (friction 15)
- Region: NA (modifier 0)
- Health delta: -48% usage last 90d, 3 P1 tickets -> offset -16
- Priority score = 30+22+15+0-16 = 51 -> Medium
- Actions: 1) Emergency tech deep-dive with SEs to triage P1s (by EOD+7), 2) propose targeted cost-performance plan (quantization + burst config), 3) schedule exec check-in week of renewal
- Suggested owners: CSM + Solutions Eng + AM
- Renewal: 2026-01-15, auto-renew clause? no
- Estimated NRR impact: $0-$420k (high risk)

2) Atlas Fintech (Strategic)
- Owner: Jordan Lee
- ARR: $2.1M
- Tier: S (40)
- ICP fit: 24
- Deployment: Private on-prem (20)
- Region: EMEA (modifier +2 due to audit window)
- Health delta: +12% usage, zero critical tickets -> offset +6
- Priority score = 40+24+20+2+6 = 92 -> High
- Actions: 1) Formal renewal proposal + 2% discount for 24m commit, 2) engineer-led uptime review to lock SLA, 3) secure C-level intro for reference expansion
- Estimated NRR impact: $1.8M-$2.2M (expansion opportunity)

3) LearningLoop (Small growth)
- Owner: Priya Nair
- ARR: $72k
- Tier: C (10)
- ICP fit: 12
- Deployment: Hosted (5)
- Region: APAC (modifier +3 due to billing cadence)
- Health delta: +1% usage, 0 tickets -> offset 0
- Priority score = 10+12+5+3+0 = 30 -> Low
- Actions: 1) Standard renewal outreach, 2) include product education workshop for adoption, 3) no exec outreach unless usage changes
- Estimated NRR impact: $0-$72k

Segmentation playbook (by bucket):
- High priority (score >=70):
  - Tactics: Exec-level engagements, formal renewal offers, dedicated SRE/SE time allocation, use legal & AM for expedited contract. Aim: protect ARR and convert expansion signals.
  - Expected cadence: weekly syncs until renewal closed.
  - KPIs: Signed renewal or upsell within 60 days, reduction in critical tickets to 0 within 14 days.

- Medium priority (45-69):
  - Tactics: Technical remediation plan + customer success value review. Consider limited commercial concessions tied to 12-24 month commit.
  - Expected cadence: biweekly triage + targeted exec touchpoint if remediation fails.
  - KPIs: Usage recovery to baseline within 30 days, commit to roadmap item or pilot.

- Low priority (<45):
  - Tactics: Standard renewal play, automation for outreach, enablement content. Monitor for signal changes.
  - Expected cadence: monthly check-ins, enablement campaigns.
  - KPIs: Renewal retained at same ARR or customer moved to self-serve path.

Quick triage checklist for upcoming QBR prep (7 days before):
- Confirm latest usage metrics and ticket backlog (SRE/Support snapshot).
- Verify legal contract window and any outstanding PO/Procurement blockers.
- Capture exec interest flags (sales notes + AM).
- Run 1-page health summary (usage trend, latency/SLO breaches, top 3 blockers).
- Prepare 2 recommendations (one technical, one commercial) with required sign-offs.

Playbook actions mapped to owners (short):
- CSM: account health narrative, primary communication, exec calendaring.
- Solutions Eng: deep dive, P1 remediation plan, performance tuning.
- Platform/Infra Eng on-call: investigate SLO/latency anomalies.
- AM/AE: commercial offer, contract negotiation, channel with Legal.
- Customer Success Ops: update segmentation sheet, track playbook completion status.

Operational notes & integration points:
- Export snapshots weekly to the QBR deck template: CONFLUENCE: /QBR Templates Master.
- Link tickets: prefer Jira keys in the notes column (e.g., CSUP-3129).
- For dedicated/private customers, ensure security reviewer is looped 30d prior to renewal to surface compliance blockers.
- Use the "renewal-watch" Slack channel for escalations; tag @reduction-oncall for infra incidents.

Open questions & next steps for this doc:
- Weighting sanity check: propose a review with Go-to-Market (AM lead) to validate commercial concessions logic (target: by 2026-03-01).
- Automation: CS Ops to prototype a formulaic export from product analytics to populate usage delta and ticket counts (owner: Priya Nair).
- Regional nuances: build APAC and EMEA sub-rows for fiscal/PO cadence.

Appendix A — Short guidance on ICP fit scoring (examples):
- 0-8: Adjacent use-case, high rework to product fit (e.g., one-off connectors).
- 9-16: Partial fit — uses core features but needs custom integration.
- 17-21: Strong fit — standard product maps to most workflows.
- 22-25: Ideal strategic fit — referenceable, joint-marketing potential.

Appendix B — Suggested sheet filters and conditional formatting:
- Highlight High priority rows red, Medium amber, Low green.
- Sort view: Priority bucket desc, then Renewal date asc.
- Filter: Deployment mode = Private -> show only accounts with SLAs expiring within 180d.

Document history / notes:
- Created by: Sofia Ramirez (CS) 2025-11-03 as an attempt to standardize QBR prioritization across regions.
- Iterations: 2026-01-12 (added region modifiers), 2026-02-18 (health offset logic refined after triage run).

Notes to reviewers:
- Please add regional exceptions and one example account from your book to the sample rows so we can run a pilot for the March QBR cycle.
- If you disagree with weights, add a comment with suggested new weights and rationale.
